subject: Prompt/Response Handover + Subprocessor Gating — DPA amendment scope
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@healthora.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthora.com; jamie.li@healthora.com
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data-use boundaries + subprocessors — Healthora pilot

Hi Logan,

Quick intro — I'm Elena (PM at Healthora). We're evaluating Redwood for a clinical intake pilot and our legal/privacy team needs clarity on a couple of items before we proceed:

1) Can Redwood commit contractually that Healthora prompts and model responses will not be used to improve or retrain Redwood models (no-training/no-derive)? If not a permanent ban, what operational guards (e.g., transient KV, ephemeral sessions, explicit opt-out flags) can you offer?

2) We need a current subprocessor roster and a description of any cross-border transfer paths (e.g., telemetry, logs, backups).

3) Evidence we can point to in the DPA amendment: an attestation of non-training, a short ops runbook for prompt redaction/retention, and KMS/residency commitments for onshore keys.

We have an internal contracting milestone next week — can you respond with a proposed amendment or redlines + an evidence checklist by EOD Friday? Attaching our standard procurement questionnaire separately.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Product Lead, Healthora
elena.park@healthora.com

[Attachment: procurement_questionnaire_healthora.pdf]

From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@healthora.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data-use boundaries + subprocessors — Healthora pilot

Elena — great to meet you over email. Thanks for laying out the asks. Below is what we can commit and what we'll propose as an amendment (high level) by Friday:

- Contract commitment: Redwood can offer a "no-model-improvement" clause scoped to Healthora tenant data (prompts + responses) for production traffic tied to the pilot. We need to align on definition of "use for model improvement" (training, fine-tuning, benchmarking).

- Operational controls: ephemeral KV cache for session context, configurable capture toggles (per-tenant), and an opt-out flag at the API level that routes requests to a segregated processing lane where model updates are blocked.

- Subprocessors & transfers: attaching our canonical subprocessor CSV and a draft DPA amendment (v1) that includes an exportability statement and KMS residency options (bring-your-own-key or Redwood-managed with US-only keying).

- Evidence pack: short attestation doc + a 1-page ops checklist (retention window, redaction guidance, SFTP export lane). We'll include a dated attestation signed by our security lead.

Action items from Redwood by EOD Fri: DPA_Amendment_v1.docx, subprocessor_list_20261007.csv, evidence_checklist.pdf.

If Healthora wants an escrow-style custody approach for prompts/responses (so requests/outputs are stored in a customer-controlled escrow), we can sketch that but it likely requires a procurement addendum.

I'll loop Marissa on the ops details (she's handling evidence flow) and Kim on the contract language.

Best,
Logan Wright
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

[Attachments: DPA_Amendment_v1.docx; subprocessor_list_20261007.csv; evidence_checklist.pdf]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data-use boundaries + subprocessors — Healthora pilot

Adding a couple operational clarifications for the evidence checklist:

- Ephemeral KV: confirm TTL semantics (we propose default 30s with a max configurable 24h for transactional sessions) and a delete-on-export API endpoint.
- Capture toggles: document per-route and per-API-key toggles + SDK flags to support front-end opt-out.
- Audit trail: include token-level logs showing route selection (segregated lane vs standard) and a small sample log export (sanitized) to show residency routing.
- SFTP export lane: checklist should describe proof-of-exports (checksums + timestamps) and retention purge records.

I'll prepare the operational one-pager and a sanitized sample log for Healthora's privacy team. Leaning toward a short MAP (mutual action plan) — if they approve the amendment we can start a 2-week tech enablement to wire the toggles and verify exports.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

[Attachment: opsevidence_onepager_draft.pdf]

From: Jamie Li <jamie.li@healthora.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@healthora.com>; procurement@healthora.com
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data-use boundaries + subprocessors — Healthora pilot

Logan / team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Couple of follow-ups from legal:

- Definition: we need a tight definition of "healthora tenant data" in the amendment (customer-controlled input and any engine outputs tied to that input). Can Redwood accept that language and also include an explicit clause that prohibits using that data for model benchmarking or public evaluations?

- Evidence: redlines attached (see redlines_healthora_v1.docx). We'd prefer a short attestation signed by the Head of Security and a runbook excerpt rather than a full ops SOP.

- Timeline: procurement requires signed amendment or fully agreed-upon redlines by Tue COB to hit our pilot go/no-go. Is that feasible?

Thanks — Jamie
Jamie Li
Sr. Counsel, Healthora
jamie.li@healthora.com

[Attachments: redlines_healthora_v1.docx]

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Jamie Li <jamie.li@healthora.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@healthora.com>
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data-use boundaries + subprocessors — Healthora pilot

Jamie / Elena — thanks for the redlines. Quick legal response:

- Definition: Redwood agrees to define "Healthora tenant data" as (i) inputs submitted by Healthora or its end users under the account; and (ii) direct model outputs generated in response to those inputs. We will add an explicit prohibition on using that data for benchmarking, benchmarking datasets, or public evaluation without explicit written consent.

- Scope & carveouts: We need to preserve telemetry that is necessary for operational stability (e.g., request rate, error traces) in an anonymized/aggregated form for debugging. We'll add an exception limited to aggregated performance metrics that cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct inputs/outputs.

- Evidence: we'll provide a signed attestation (Head of Security), a 1-page runbook excerpt for the capture toggle and TTL workflow, and a sanitized sample export log. For escrow-style custody: we can offer a model that (a) deposits raw interactions in a customer-controlled SFTP for the pilot period; or (b) retains them encrypted with BYOK where Healthora holds the key and Redwood cannot decrypt for training. Both will require a brief implementation window.

Next steps: Redwood will accept Healthora redlines with minor edits and circulate DPA_Amendment_v1_redlined.docx by EOD Mon. Can we confirm a final signoff window Tue COB?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

[Attachment: proposed_attestation_security_signed.pdf]
